title: MYASTHENIC SYNDROME, CONGENITAL, 11, ASSOCIATED WITH ACETYLCHOLINE RECEPTOR DEFICIENCY

relationships.phenotype: MYASTHENIC SYNDROME, CONGENITAL, 11, ASSOCIATED WITH ACETYLCHOLINE RECEPTOR DEFICIENCY

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital myasthenic syndrome-11 associated with acetylcholine receptor deficiency (CMS11) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding rapsyn (RAPSN).

checks.claim: Congenital myasthenic syndrome-11 associated with acetylcholine receptor deficiency (CMS11) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the RAPSN gene, which encodes rapsyn.
checks.evidence_quote: we identify three recessive rapsyn mutations: one patient carries L14P in TPR1 and N88K in TPR3; two are homozygous for N88K; and one carries N88K and 553ins5
checks.explanation: Recessive homozygous and compound heterozygous rapsyn mutations in patients with endplate AChR deficiency. The CMS11 label is the entry's own disease name and does not appear in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: CMS11 is an autosomal recessive congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by deficiency of the postsynaptic protein rapsyn. Rapsyn is needed to cluster acetylcholine receptor (AChR) at the motor endplate, and its deficiency causes endplate AChR deficiency (Ohno et al., 2002; Engel et al., 2015). Engel et al. (2015) stated that most patients presented in the first year of life and a few later in life. Arthrogryposis and other congenital malformations occurred in nearly one-third of patients, and intercurrent infections or fever could trigger respiratory crises. Most patients responded well to acetylcholinesterase inhibitors.

checks.evidence_quote: In four patients with EP AChR deficiency but with no mutations in AChR subunits, we identify three recessive rapsyn mutations
checks.explanation: The abstract describes recessive rapsyn mutations that reduce rapsyn at the endplate in a congenital myasthenic syndrome.

checks.evidence_quote: Rapsyn, a 43-kDa postsynaptic protein, plays an essential role in the clustering of AChR at the EP.

checks.evidence_quote: Rapsyn mutations in humans cause endplate acetylcholine-receptor deficiency and myasthenic syndrome.
checks.explanation: Stated in the title. The abstract's endplate studies also show decreased rapsyn and AChR.

paragraphs.text: Goldhammer et al. (1990) described 14 Jewish patients from 10 families of Iraqi or Iranian origin with congenital myasthenia and facial malformations. The malformations included an elongated face, mandibular prognathism with class III malocclusion, and a high-arched palate. Muscle weakness was mainly limited to ptosis, weakness of the facial and masticatory muscles, and fatigable speech. The course was mild and nonprogressive, and the patients responded to cholinesterase inhibitors. They had no antibodies to acetylcholine receptor. Repetitive stimulation at 3 Hz produced a decremental response, but a single nerve stimulus did not evoke a repetitive compound muscle action potential. The authors suggested that the facial abnormalities might be secondary to the neuromuscular defect, or might be primary and unrelated to it.

paragraphs.text: Burke et al. (2003) studied 16 unrelated patients with congenital or hereditary myasthenic syndrome due to rapsyn mutations and identified 2 distinct phenotypes, one with early onset and one with late onset. The early-onset form was frequently associated with arthrogryposis multiplex congenita and life-threatening crises. The late-onset form developed in adolescence or adulthood and was initially mistaken for seronegative myasthenia gravis.

paragraphs.text: Das et al. (2014) reported a 20-month-old boy with rapsyn deficiency. At birth he had a weak cry, hypotonia, joint contractures, and facial deformity. Because of respiratory difficulty associated with muscle fatigue, he spent a total of 71 days in the neonatal intensive care unit and 47 days in the pediatric intensive care unit. Imaging, metabolic tests, and electrodiagnostic studies were normal. A muscle biopsy showed myofiber atrophy in a pattern consistent with early denervation.

paragraphs.text: In a review, Engel et al. (2015) noted that the clinical features of rapsyn deficiency can suggest autoimmune myasthenia gravis, but ocular ductions are intact in most patients. Apneic episodes occur in some patients with rapsyn mutations. Endplate studies show multiple synaptic contacts on single muscle fibers. The endplate AChR deficiency is milder than in primary AChR deficiency, and the junctional folds are poorly differentiated. In the Mayo Clinic cohort of patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome investigated between 1988 and 2014, rapsyn deficiency accounted for 51 index cases (14.3%).

paragraphs.text: Menold et al. (1998) studied 5 families of Iranian Jewish origin with a phenotypically distinct form of congenital myasthenic syndrome. The families included 6 affected individuals, 4 of the families were consanguineous, and all came from the same geographic region. Linkage analysis excluded the regions on chromosomes 2 and 17 that contain the AChR subunit genes. It also excluded the region on 17p to which familial infantile myasthenia had been mapped. The authors concluded that a defect in a different gene caused the disorder in these patients.

paragraphs.text: Ohno et al. (2002) studied 4 patients with endplate AChR deficiency who had no mutations in the AChR subunit genes. In all 4 they identified recessive mutations in the RAPSN gene. One patient was compound heterozygous for L14P in the first tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR1) and N88K in TPR3. Two patients were homozygous for N88K. One patient was compound heterozygous for N88K and a 5-bp insertion (553ins5) that causes a frameshift in TPR5. Endplate studies in each patient showed reduced staining for rapsyn and AChR, as well as impaired postsynaptic morphologic development. Expression studies in HEK cells showed that none of the mutations impaired rapsyn self-association, but all 3 reduced coclustering of AChR with rapsyn.

paragraphs.text: Ohno et al. (2003) identified 2 mutations in E-boxes in the RAPSN promoter region in 8 patients with congenital myasthenic syndrome. Patient 1 carried a -27C-G mutation that changes the E-box at positions -27 to -22 from CAGCTG to GAGCTG, and the allele carrying it was not transcribed in the patient's muscle. Patients 2 through 8 were Oriental Jews of Iraqi or Iranian origin with facial malformations. They carried a -38A-G mutation that changes another E-box, at positions -40 to -35, from CAACTG to CAGCTG without altering the CANNTG consensus. Haplotype analysis showed that -38A-G arose from a common founder. In electrophoretic mobility shift assays, -38A-G gained and -27C-G lost binding affinity for components of nuclear extracts from C2C12 myotubes. In luciferase reporter assays, both mutations reduced reporter gene expression in C2C12 myotubes.

paragraphs.text: The boy reported by Das et al. (2014) was started on pyridostigmine at 16 months of age. His muscle tone and strength improved dramatically and his joint contractures steadily resolved. Four months after starting treatment he was beginning to bear weight, could sit unsupported, and could vocalize full words. Engel et al. (2015) stated that most patients with rapsyn deficiency respond well to acetylcholinesterase inhibitors. Some gain additional benefit from 3,4-diaminopyridine, and some benefit from adding ephedrine or albuterol.

paragraphs.text: Dunne and Maselli (2004) characterized the haplotype associated with the N88K mutation using 7 intragenic SNPs spanning 8 kb. They found a common haplotype in 3 affected N88K homozygotes that was also present in all heterozygous carriers of N88K, which supported a founder effect. Two asymptomatic individuals homozygous for N88K carried a second haplotype that differed at 3 SNP sites downstream of the mutation. The authors suggested that recombination within the rapsyn gene might have implications for the phenotypic expression of the disease.

paragraphs.text: Ohno et al. (2003) identified a -38A-G mutation in the RAPSN promoter in 7 patients (patients 2-8) with congenital myasthenic syndrome. The patients were Oriental Jews of Iraqi or Iranian origin with facial malformations. The mutation changes an E-box at positions -40 to -35 from CAACTG to CAGCTG, which does not affect the CANNTG consensus sequence. Haplotype analysis showed that the mutation arose from a common founder. The mutation gained binding affinity for components of C2C12 myotube nuclear extracts and reduced reporter gene expression in C2C12 myotubes.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with congenital myasthenic syndrome (patient 1), Ohno et al. (2003) identified a -27C-G mutation in the RAPSN promoter. The mutation changes an E-box at positions -27 to -22 from CAGCTG to GAGCTG, and the allele carrying it was not transcribed in the patient's muscle. In functional studies, the mutation lost binding affinity for components of C2C12 myotube nuclear extracts. It reduced reporter gene expression in C2C12 myotubes and in HEK cells transfected with MyoD or myogenin, and it markedly reduced the enhancer activity of an E-box on an SV40 promoter.

agent.process_note: I read the index and all 11 paper files. Ten were abstracts only, and Muller et al. (2004) was title only. For the one full text (Engel et al., 2015, a review), I used Grep to find every passage on rapsyn, RAPSN, N88K, E-box, Jewish patients and treatment, then read the rapsyn deficiency section, the cohort table and the pharmacotherapy table in full. No HGNC reference data was supplied, so the intro leaves out the RAPSN MIM number and chromosome location. Some things I looked for are not in the evidence. The abstracts give no zygosity for the -27C-G patient and do not name the 2 mutations found by Das et al. (2014). The zygosity of the -38A-G mutation comes only from Engel et al. (2015), who call it homozygous. The multiexon deletions reported by Gaudon et al. (2010) are not specified in the abstract. Nucleotide-level HGVS for N88K, L14P and 553ins5 is not given. For these reasons the Das and Gaudon variants were not listed as allelic variants.
